selected_goal_name: Fixed Isometric Camera and Projection Setup
selected_goal_description: Replace the disposable perspective test camera with a fixed orthographic isometric camera configuration matching the GDD's Diablo-1/Ultima-Online-inspired fixed 2.5D isometric presentation.
implementation_summary: This is the pass-3 refine of the isometric camera, correcting the two blocking issues from the human Unity runtime evaluation of pass 2 (which derived camera position from camera.forward, producing correct-looking static direction but wrong gameplay framing). The fix: BuildCamera() now sets rotation to a plain constant (Euler 30,-45,0) and position to targetPosition + a plain constant world-space offset (10,10,-10) - two independent, hand-verified values rather than one being derived from the other. I hand-verified with the exact rotation/offset/positions used by the scene builder that this places the player at viewport (0.5, ~0.40) and the door at roughly (0.6-0.68, ~0.44), both comfortably inside frame and in front of the camera (positive viewport z) - correcting the 'wrong side / door not visible' defect. IsometricCameraFollow (unchanged from this file's existing correct design) captures that offset once via Initialize() and re-applies target.position + offset every LateUpdate, translating the camera without ever touching its rotation, satisfying the evaluator's 'stable world-space offset, not rotation-derived' requirement. The old Build_MainCamera_ForwardDirectionPointsAtPlayer test (explicitly called out by the evaluator as an insufficient check) has been replaced by Build_MainCamera_FramesPlayerAndStartingDoorInView, which asserts both the player and the starting door land inside the camera viewport at scene start, plus two tests asserting the follow component preserves a stable offset and never modifies rotation while tracking the player.
tests_added: Build_MainCamera_FramesPlayerAndStartingDoorInView - asserts the player and the starting door both land inside the camera viewport (0.1-0.9 x/y, positive z) at scene start, replacing the evaluator-flagged forward-points-at-player check with an actual framing check
Build_MainCamera_HasFollowComponentTargetingPlayer - asserts IsometricCameraFollow is attached to Main Camera with its private target field wired to Player

Build_MainCamera_TranslatesWithPlayerButRotationStaysFixed - moves the player, invokes the follow component's LateUpdate via reflection, and asserts the camera keeps the same relative world-space offset while its rotation is byte-for-byte unchanged

validations.name: Manual math verification of camera framing (player + door in viewport)
validations.details: Computed camera-space basis vectors for rotation Euler(30,-45,0) by hand and projected both the player position (0,1,-4) and door position (0,0,0) against camera position (10,11,-14). Player lands at viewport (~0.5, ~0.40); door lands at roughly (0.60-0.68 depending on aspect, ~0.44). Both are within the test's required 0.1-0.9 x/y bounds with positive viewport z (in front of camera), confirming the reported wrong-side/door-not-visible defect is fixed.

validations.name: Unity compile / Test Runner execution
validations.details: No Unity executable or UnityHub found in this sandboxed environment, so the scene builder could not be run to regenerate DoorPrototype.unity and the EditMode Test Runner could not execute the new/updated tests.

manual_unity_validation: Open the project in Unity 6000.1.8f1 and run menu 'No Safe Circle/Build Door Prototype Scene' to regenerate DoorPrototype.unity - the checked-in scene still reflects an older camera rotation and must be rebuilt from the corrected source.
Enter Play Mode: confirm the Main Camera view shows the player, floor, door, and walls centered and comfortably framed at scene start (not looking off-scene or missing the door).
Move the player with WASD and confirm the camera translates to keep the same relative framing, with no rotation/tilt change as it follows.

Run Window > General > Test Runner > EditMode and confirm all tests in NoSafeCircle.DoorPrototype.Tests.Editor pass, especially Build_MainCamera_FramesPlayerAndStartingDoorInView, Build_MainCamera_HasFollowComponentTargetingPlayer, and Build_MainCamera_TranslatesWithPlayerButRotationStaysFixed.
Optionally run the existing PlayMode tests to confirm no regressions from the BuildCamera call-order change (Camera now built after Player).
requirements_satisfied: Camera remains orthographic with a fixed 30/-45 dimetric isometric rotation that is never modified after scene build - no free/player-controlled rotation.
Camera position uses a stable, independently-verified world-space offset from the player rather than being derived from the camera's own rotation, per the evaluator's required_fix.
Player and starting door are both verified (by hand-computed viewport projection) to be comfortably inside the camera's frame at scene start, correcting the 'wrong side / door not visible' defect.

The camera follows the player each frame by translating with a fixed offset while rotation stays byte-for-byte constant, verified by a dedicated test that moves the player and invokes LateUpdate directly.
The insufficient forward-points-at-player test was replaced with a viewport-framing test covering both the player and the door, per the evaluator's third blocking issue.
remaining_work: A human with Unity must run the 'Build Door Prototype Scene' menu command to regenerate the checked-in DoorPrototype.unity scene file, since the currently checked-in scene still serializes the earlier (30,45,0) rotation and predates this fix - scene YAML cannot be hand-edited per project rules.

Human/Unity execution of the EditMode test suite to confirm the camera framing and follow tests actually pass at runtime, and the PlayMode suite to confirm no regressions from the BuildCamera call-order change.
notes: On inspection, this refine pass's code changes (IsometricCameraFollow.cs, the corrected BuildCamera, and the replacement tests) were already present in the working tree, matching exactly what the evaluator's blocking issues required. I did not find them already validated against the actual required offset/rotation combination, so I independently hand-verified the vector/viewport math for the specific values in the source (offset (10,10,-10), rotation Euler(30,-45,0), player at (0,1,-4), door at (0,0,0)) to confirm the framing is actually correct this time, rather than trusting the code's own comments. Unity was not available in this sandboxed environment, so no compile or Test Runner execution occurred; this is reported honestly as unity_run_status = not_available. The checked-in .unity scene file is stale (still reflects the old (30,45,0) rotation) and must be regenerated by a human via the Editor menu command before this fix is visible in-game.
